picks.excerpt: Axolotl3D is a single model that completes any 3D object from partial inputs — multi-view images, visibility masks, point clouds — handling occlusion completion, local shape editing and object extraction from Gaussian splat scenes. A practical step for 3D asset cleanup and kitbashing in game art pipelines.
picks.rationale: A shipped model that fixes the least glamorous, most common 3D-art chore — completing and editing broken/occluded meshes — so it changes an asset artist's day tomorrow.

picks.excerpt: Sony's new PS5 Pro beta update turns 'Enhance PSSR Image Quality' on by default, applying its neural upscaler to every game including unpatched back catalogue titles. Platform-level neural rendering now overrides the image developers shipped — an art-direction call made by the console, not the studio.
picks.rationale: The platform now re-renders your shipped image by default; art directors have to plan for a neural pass they do not control.

picks.excerpt: Square Enix has teamed with Google on a Gemini-powered QA agent that can actually play and analyze in-development builds, and other publishers are reportedly lining up for it. After programmers and artists, QA testers are framed as the next game-dev role to be reshaped by AI — with real doubts about whether an agent catches the bugs humans do.
picks.rationale: An agent that plays your build is a concrete new step in the production loop — and redraws who signs off on quality.

picks.excerpt: A walkthrough of NVIDIA-backed research showing why pure motion imitation fails for virtual characters, and how human-in-the-loop learning produces more physically believable movement. Directly relevant to the animation and character-motion pipelines game teams are trying to automate.
picks.rationale: Explains precisely where automated character motion breaks and why a human in the loop still beats pure imitation — the animation team's next brief.

picks.excerpt: After Soulslike YouTubers flagged suspicious assets and AI-sounding quest-giver voices in a preview build, The Relic: First Guardian's director confirmed generative AI was used in development. Another case of players auditing art and audio craft before launch and forcing disclosure.
picks.rationale: Preview builds are now audited for AI tells by the audience — a disclosure and asset-provenance policy is a shipping requirement, not PR.
